messages:
customer_acme: Hey team — since upgrading to @redwood-inference-js 1.4.0 our Next.js SSR endpoints intermittently get 401s from the /v1/generate API. Happens ~1 in 10 requests. No code changes otherwise. Anyone seen this?

support_jen: Sorry you're hitting that, can you share a minimal repro / package.json + how you're bundling? 401 usually means Authorization header missing or malformed.

customer_acme: Repro: Next 13 -> Node 18, using default nextjs build. package.json snippet:```json
{
  "dependencies": {
    "redwood-inference": "^1.4.0"
  },
  "type": "module"
}
```
Error stack (serverless SSR):```
Error: 401 Unauthorized
    at fetch (node_modules/node-fetch/index.js:... )
    at /workspace/.next/server/pages/api/generate.js:45:12
```
On 1.3.2 it was fine. Rolling back helps immediately.

support_jen: Thanks. Two quick asks: 1) paste how you import the SDK, 2) can you try `npm i redwood-inference@1.4.0 && NODE_ENV=production next build && NODE_ENV=production next start` to reproduce prod build?

customer_acme: Import: `import Redwood from 'redwood-inference'` (default import). I did a production build — still repros. I also tried `import * as Redwood from 'redwood-inference'` — same flakiness.

support_jen: Ack. Looping in devex + eng. @devex_miguel @eng_alex can you triage, seems like packaging/exports/runtime interop.

devex_miguel: tagging in. Do you have a small repo we can run? If not, can you run `node -e "console.log(require.resolve('redwood-inference'))"` in your app dir (after building) and paste result? That helps us see which entry the bundler picked.

customer_acme: Ran it in a fresh container after `next build` and `next start`: `/workspace/node_modules/redwood-inference/dist/cjs/index.js`

eng_alex: That path is suspicious — bundler should prefer ESM entry for modern apps. Looks like Node/Next picked the CJS build. In recent SDK versions we changed how headers are attached in the runtime for ESM vs CJS (small shim). If the CJS build runs in an ESM-ish environment the auth wrapper can be skipped, resulting in missing Authorization.

eng_alex: Short term workaround: import the ESM entry explicitly: `import Redwood from 'redwood-inference/dist/esm/index.mjs'` or set in next.config.js:```js
module.exports = {
  experimental: { esmExternals: true }
}
```
Both should force the ESM code path and avoid the header-mismatch.

customer_acme: Importing dist/esm fixes it in our test env — no 401s so far. Not ideal as a long-term fix.

devex_miguel: We're going to publish a patch to make the package exports map explicit so bundlers don't accidentally pick the CJS entry for ESM apps. Can you confirm what bundler Next uses in your environment (webpack or turbopack)?

customer_acme: Using turbopack in Node 18.

eng_alex: Turbopack + `type: module` can prefer CJS in some resolution edge cases we didn't hit in earlier releases. We'll reproduce with turbopack and Next. Also adding @deploy-bot to record rollout.

deploy-bot: Deploy action: created issue RW-3812 in internal tracker for packaging/exports + turbopack. Priority: P1 -> triage required.

eng_alex: Repro steps I used locally (fast):
1) clone minimal repro: internal/gists/sku-redwood-repro (sent privately)
2) `npm i && NODE_OPTIONS=--enable-source-maps npm run build`
3) run `node -e "console.log(require.resolve('redwood-inference'))"` -> shows `dist/cjs/index.js`
4) reproduce 401 in SSR route when using default import

eng_alex: Root cause summary: package.json conditional exports didn't include an explicit "import" subpath for the main entry that turbopack/next resolves in this combination, so the bundler fell back to the CJS file. The CJS entry relies on a runtime shim loaded only when the Node loader detects pure CommonJS flow. When that shim is skipped (mixed environment), the Authorization header attach logic is a no-op in some requests, producing intermittent 401s under burst load.

eng_alex: Fix planned: in 1.4.1 we'll update package.json exports to include explicit mappings: "./": { "import": "./dist/esm/index.mjs", "require": "./dist/cjs/index.js" } and add a small runtime guard so both builds attach auth consistently.

support_jen: ETA on release? Any customer-facing config we should tell users to set meanwhile?

eng_alex: We'll cut 1.4.1 in the next 6 hours. For customers: either pin to 1.3.2 (safe), or use the explicit ESM import workaround noted above, or set `experimental.esmExternals: true` in next.config.js if you can. We'll publish a security/compatibility note once 1.4.1 is out.

customer_acme: Thanks — we'll pin to 1.3.2 for now and test the ESM import workaround in staging. Please ping when 1.4.1 is out and we'll validate.

devex_miguel: Thanks for quick repro and for validating the workaround. @eng_alex please include the repro link in the patch so QA can run with turbopack.

eng_alex: Will do. Patch will include unit test that asserts `require.resolve()` for a minimal app returns the `dist/esm/index.mjs` path under typical modern configs.

deploy-bot: Release pipeline: created release candidate 1.4.1-rc.1 targeting main.

support_jen: Noting on the ticket: workaround + rollback options sent to customer. Will follow up after rc1 passes. :thumbsup:

customer_acme: Received, thanks everyone. Appreciate the quick turnaround.

eng_alex: Follow-up: 1.4.1 published and rolled out. Patch notes: exports map explicit, runtime auth guard added, no behavior changes otherwise. Please test and re-open if you still hit anything.

customer_acme: Confirmed — upgraded to 1.4.1, ran prod build, no 401s after 1 hour of soak. Closing on our side.

support_jen: Closing thread. If anyone else sees similar, tag #support or reopen RW-3812.
